payload.title: The baseline exam derives scanned_sha only from the evidence_envelopes of the runs that kept them (7 of 17 in the kept store) and never reads each row's repo_snapshot, so a working-tree scan with uncommitted changes is stamped as a clean scan of the commit and the report does not say which runs back the tree it names
evidence: tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:739-745 (scanned is the set of envelope target_sha values; a row with no envelopes contributes nothing and is not named)
tools/aria-acceptance/harness.py:748-759 (the single scanned sha must equal the corpus head and --aria-sha; dirty_snapshot and repo_state_id are not consulted)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/tool_runner.py:365-377 (the compact snapshot holds dirty_snapshot and repo_state_id)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/snapshot.py:104-111 (in working_tree mode base_commit_sha is HEAD while dirty_snapshot is true when files are modified)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/evidence_validator.py:1167-1171 (an envelope's target_sha is taken from the snapshot's base_commit_sha)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/ledger_inline.py:33-40 (a spilled evidence_validation keeps no envelopes, which is why most rows carry none)
payload.rule_violated: F1.3: every number is stamped with the ARIA SHA it was measured at; the stamp must be refused when the run did not scan that commit's clean tree.
payload.notes: A cycle scanned in working_tree mode (not the committed mode) over a checkout with uncommitted edits records, for each run that kept envelopes, target_sha = HEAD and dirty_snapshot = true. The exam sees one scanned sha equal to the corpus head and --aria-sha and accepts it, so a tally measured on modified code is stamped as the measurement of that commit. The evidence reviewer set dirty_snapshot true on all 17 rows of a store copy and the exam exited 0 with the same stamp. The evidence reviewer found that in the kept store ten of the 17 runs (including the 250-finding doc-staleness run and the kernel-dead-wire run behind 7 of the 29 named noise) have no envelope, so the tree claim is backed by 7 runs while the report states one store.scanned_sha for the cycle. Close condition: Require, over every run of the cycle, repo_snapshot.dirty_snapshot is False and a single repo_state_id (refuse by name otherwise), and record in the report which tools evidence the scanned tree and which do not. Add tests: all rows dirty_snapshot true is refused; two repo_state_id values is refused; a spilled row is listed as not evidencing the tree. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
